entries.title: How plants make their own food
entries.answer: A green plant uses sunlight, water, and a gas called carbon dioxide to make sugar. This is photosynthesis. In many plants most of the work happens in the leaves. A green material called chlorophyll helps catch energy from light. With that energy, the plant makes sugars it can use to grow or store for later. During this process the plant also gives off oxygen. The water usually comes from the soil, and the carbon dioxide enters the plant from the air.
facts: Chlorophyll helps give many leaves their green color.
Many algae use light to make sugars too.

entries.title: How pollen travels from flower to flower
entries.answer: Flowers can make tiny grains called pollen. For many flowers to make seeds, pollen must reach a part of a flower that can receive it. Moving pollen there is called pollination. A bee that visits a flower for food can pick up pollen on its body. On the next flower, some grains can rub off. Some plants use wind to move pollen instead. Plants often need a match between the kind of pollen and the kind of flower, so pollen landing anywhere is only one step in making seeds.
facts: Wind can carry pollen from some kinds of plants.
Bees are not the only animals that can carry pollen.

entries.title: How seeds start new plants
entries.answer: A seed holds the beginnings of a new plant. A coat helps protect the tiny plant inside. Many seeds also hold food that the young plant can use before it has leaves. With the right conditions, a seed can start to grow. Some seeds are carried by the wind. Others hitch a ride on an animal’s fur or travel inside a fruit that an animal eats. When a seed ends up far from its parent, the new plant may get more light or space to grow.
facts: Some seeds can travel by water.
Germination is the beginning of a seed’s growth.
